entities.title: Exact i128 arithmetic, refusing what doesn't fit
entities.summary: Years and day counts are i128 and fractions reduced i128 rationals, every step checked; beyond that range the answer is unsupported (implementation-limit).
entities.context: UTV requires arbitrary precision: integers are decimal strings and fractions exact rationals. The contract lets each language choose its integer type: BigInteger in C# and Java, int in Python, bigint in TypeScript, i128 in Rust.
entities.decision: Checked i128 everywhere (num.rs Q, days_from_civil, civil_from_days); an overflow is None, reported as unsupported with implementation-limit.
entities.rationale: "Years are arbitrary precision ... i128 in Rust, where anything beyond the range gives unsupported with implementation-limit" (docs/library-api.md section 1); "anything beyond is unsupported (implementation-limit), never a wrapped value" (README, The JSON layer).

relationships.description: Meets it within i128, and refuses beyond.

entities.title: The Gregorian check is a separate function
entities.summary: validate_structural no longer judges dates; validate_gregorian_civil does, as its own question.
entities.context: Until 0.2.0, validate_structural also ran the Gregorian date check, so 30 February was structurally invalid.
entities.decision: validate_structural checks the envelope and schema only; validate_gregorian_civil runs it first and then checks month and day, answering unsupported for other kinds and calendars.
entities.rationale: "Structural and semantic validation are separate questions" (CHANGELOG 0.2.0; validate_gregorian_civil's documentation cites implementations/README.md).

entities.title: A strict JSON parser for validation and rule bundles
entities.summary: JSON text is parsed through a custom serde visitor that refuses a repeated object key, which serde_json alone accepts.
entities.context: serde_json keeps the last value of a repeated key (tests/native_first/json.rs shows it). UTV libraries must fail closed on duplicate JSON keys.
entities.decision: parse_strict and the validators parse through StrictVisitor; a data error from it is reported as duplicate-key, anything else as syntax (since the Unreleased changes; before, both were syntax).
entities.rationale: Fail closed on duplicate keys (implementations/README.md, obligation 7), with the shared code the other libraries report.
